topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a joint venture?
options: Two or more businesses creating a shared enterprise, sharing control, risk and reward
One business acquiring a controlling interest in another
Two businesses combining into a single new business
A cooperative agreement that involves no shared ownership
questions.why: A joint venture involves shared ownership of a new enterprise, which distinguishes it from a looser alliance.
whyNot: That is a takeover.
That is a merger.
That is a strategic alliance.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a takeover?
options: One business acquiring a controlling interest in another
Two businesses agreeing to combine as equals
A business licensing its brand to a foreign producer
A business opening a new subsidiary abroad
questions.why: A merger is agreed and creates a new combined business; a takeover is an acquisition of control.
whyNot: That is a merger.
That is licensing.
That is greenfield investment.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines synergy?
options: The idea that a combined business is worth more than the two separate businesses
The cost of integrating two businesses after a deal
The premium paid above the target's market value
The process of investigating a target before purchase
questions.why: Overestimated synergies are one of the most common causes of acquisition failure.
whyNot: That is integration cost.
That is the acquisition premium.
That is due diligence.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines due diligence?
options: Detailed investigation of a target business before an acquisition
The legal duty to treat all shareholders equally
The process of integrating two workforces
A requirement to consult employees before a merger
questions.why: Poor due diligence means liabilities, contracts or quality problems are discovered after completion.
whyNot: That is a governance duty.
That is integration.
Consultation is a separate legal obligation in some jurisdictions.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which route into a foreign market is fastest?
options: An acquisition, because customers, distribution and approvals already exist
Organic growth, because no negotiation is needed
Exporting through an agent, because no investment is required
A greenfield investment, because it is built to the business's own design
questions.why: Speed is the main attraction of acquisition, and integration is the price paid for it.
whyNot: Organic growth is the slowest route.
Exporting is quick but does not establish a market position.
Greenfield is slow and starts with no customers.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Why is local knowledge a common reason for a joint venture?
options: Customer preferences, regulation and government relationships are hard for an outsider to learn
Local partners always provide the majority of the capital
Joint ventures are cheaper than any other route
Local knowledge is required by the WTO
questions.why: It is the factor most often underestimated by confident foreign entrants and the one a local partner supplies most cheaply.
whyNot: Capital contributions are negotiated and vary.
Cost depends on the deal; the attraction is shared risk and knowledge.
The WTO imposes no such requirement.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which of the following makes a joint venture compulsory rather than chosen?
options: A country requiring foreign businesses to operate with a local partner
A shortage of capital in the acquiring business
A desire to reduce competition in the market
The need to acquire a patent
questions.why: Some countries cap foreign ownership, particularly in strategic sectors, so the joint venture is the price of entry.
whyNot: Capital shortage is a reason to prefer one, not a requirement.
That is a reason for acquisition.
A patent can be licensed or acquired.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Why might a business acquire a firm inside a trading bloc?
options: It gains tariff-free access to every member of the bloc
Acquisitions inside blocs require no regulatory approval
Bloc members pay no corporation tax
Acquisition inside a bloc removes all integration risk
questions.why: It is the fastest way to get inside the common external tariff.
whyNot: Competition authorities still review large deals.
Members set their own tax rates.
Integration risk is unaffected by location.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which of the following is the main problem with an acquisition as a growth route?
options: Integration, particularly culture clash between the two workforces
The impossibility of gaining local knowledge
The slowness of gaining market access
The inability to acquire brands or patents
questions.why: Two workforces with different attitudes to hierarchy and decision-making do not merge because a contract was signed, and it is worse across borders.
whyNot: Local knowledge is acquired with the business.
Acquisition is the fast route.
Brands and patents are among the main assets acquired.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: What is the sharpest criticism of entering a market through a joint venture?
options: Technology and know-how may be transferred to a partner who later becomes a competitor
Joint ventures require the foreign partner to pay all the costs
Joint ventures cannot be used in regulated sectors
Joint ventures provide no access to local knowledge
questions.why: In several large markets the access was real and so was the cost, as partners subsequently competed internationally.
whyNot: Costs are shared, which is the main attraction.
Regulated sectors are where they are most often required.
Local knowledge is one of the main benefits.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: What is the most common financial cause of acquisition failure?
options: Overpayment, where a premium is paid and the expected synergies do not appear
The inability to raise any finance for the deal
The target refusing to hand over its assets
Exchange rate movements on the day of completion
questions.why: Cost savings assume the two operations can actually be combined, which regulation, geography and incompatible systems may prevent.
whyNot: Deals that fail usually completed, so finance was raised.
Ownership transfers on completion.
A single day's currency movement rarely explains long-run failure.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Why is reversibility a key consideration in choosing a growth route?
options: An acquisition is very hard to unwind, while organic growth can be slowed or stopped
Reversibility determines the tax treatment of the deal
Reversible routes always generate higher returns
Only joint ventures can be reversed
questions.why: Reversibility matters most where the market is unfamiliar, because mistakes should stay small.
whyNot: Tax treatment depends on the structure, not reversibility.
Lower commitment usually means lower potential return.
A joint venture is moderately reversible; organic growth more so.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Why can diseconomies of scale arise after a global merger?
options: Coordination and communication costs rise across time zones and languages
Fixed costs increase in proportion to output
Variable costs per unit always rise after a merger
Larger businesses face higher tax rates
questions.why: Coordination problems are a standard reason the forecast savings do not materialise.
whyNot: Fixed costs are spread over more output, which is an economy.
Purchasing power usually lowers variable costs.
Tax rates do not rise with size.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Which reason for a global merger relates to competition policy risk?
options: Reducing competition by buying a rival
Sharing costs and risks on a large project
Accessing a partner's distribution network
Securing a supply of a raw material
questions.why: Large deals may be blocked or permitted only with conditions, which can remove the point of the deal.
whyNot: Cost sharing raises no competition concern.
Distribution access is usually unproblematic.
Securing supply may raise concerns only in concentrated markets.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: Why is acquiring an established brand often preferred to launching a global one?
options: Local brand loyalty can be strong and expensive to overcome
Acquired brands are always cheaper to run
Global brands cannot be registered in most countries
Acquiring a brand avoids all marketing cost
questions.why: The acquirer also gains distribution and shelf space immediately, and then faces the glocalisation question of whether to keep the local name.
whyNot: Running costs depend on the brand, not on how it was obtained.
Global brands are registered routinely.
Marketing is still required.

questions.topicTitle: Reasons for global mergers, takeovers or joint ventures
questions.stem: When should a business prefer organic growth for international expansion?
options: Where the market can be entered gradually and mistakes must stay small
Where speed is the overriding priority
Where a local partner is legally required
Where a patent must be acquired quickly
questions.why: Organic growth gives full control and the lowest risk per stage, at the cost of being slow.
whyNot: Speed points to acquisition or a joint venture.
A legal requirement points to a joint venture.
A patent usually has to be bought or licensed.
